evals.name: nextjs-ga-fonts-audit
evals.prompt: Prüfe dieses Next.js-Projekt einer Werbeagentur auf Datenschutz, bevor es live geht. Der Code liegt im Ordner evals/files/nextjs-ga-fonts. Es gibt noch keine Live-URL. Schreib den Audit-Bericht.
evals.expected_output: A German audit report (datenschutz-audit-*.md) in the Phase-4 structure. GA4 loading pre-consent and Google Fonts from the CDN are 🔴 with the right norms; the contact route is traced as a pipeline (Resend, Sentry with the body in `extra`, console.log of the body, Vercel logs in iad1); the stale OS-Plattform link is 🟠; evidence level is stated as code only, no runtime scan; the report ends with the RDG disclaimer.
expectations: A report file matching datenschutz-audit-*.md is written and contains the eight Phase-4 sections in order (Management Summary … Rechtlicher Hinweis)
GA4 (gtag.js loaded in app/layout.tsx without any consent gate) is a 🔴 finding citing § 25 Abs. 1 TDDDG and Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. a DSGVO, with the file reference app/layout.tsx
Google Fonts loaded from fonts.googleapis.com is a 🔴 finding that cites LG München I, 3 O 17493/20 and recommends self-hosting (next/font or .woff2 in the repo)

The contact form is traced as a data flow with at least these recipients: Resend, Sentry, Vercel logs — and the Datenfluss-Übersicht table names Resend as a US processor whose AVV/DPA status is ⚪️ or an open question
console.log(body) in app/api/contact/route.ts and Sentry.captureException(..., { extra: { body } }) are flagged as PII in logs / error tracking (🟠), with the file reference
The link to https://ec.europa.eu/consumers/odr in the footer is flagged as the stale OS-Plattform link (🟠, § 5 UWG), with the instruction to remove it — not to 'keep it' or 'add it'
vercel.json regions ['iad1'] is flagged: functions run in the US; recommendation fra1 (and the note that Edge Middleware is global regardless)
The hidden utm_source field forwarded in the mail is mentioned as marketing data that the DSE must cover
The Management Summary states the evidence level as 'code only / no runtime scan / no live URL' or equivalent, and the report does not claim to know what the CMP does at runtime

The report never makes its own compliance claim with 'abmahnsicher' or '100 % konform' (a warning against using such labels is fine) and the report file ends with the RDG disclaimer from references/recht.md
No Datenschutzerklärung is generated (the user asked for an audit only)

Every 🔴/🟠 finding carries an evidence line with an ID (E-xx) listed in an Evidenzverzeichnis and exactly one level (beobachtet / abgeleitet / Mandantenangabe — '⚪️ ausstehend' in place of a level fails); because there is no runtime scan, runtime behaviour (GA4 loads before consent, Google Fonts requested from Google, a page returning 404) is abgeleitet, and only what is literally in the files (code lines, config values, link targets) may be beobachtet

Section 5 assigns each recipient a role: Resend, Sentry and Vercel as Auftragsverarbeiter (Art. 28) with the AVV/DPA status left open (⚪️ / question to the client, not assumed signed); Google Fonts as a self-hosting case, not as a service needing an AVV

The Google Fonts finding rests on Art. 6 Abs. 1 DSGVO (transfer of the IP address to Google without a legal basis, LG München I) — it does not cite § 25 TDDDG as its legal basis, since loading a font neither stores nor reads information on the terminal device

The Prüftabelle / checklist part of the report covers the data-subject rights block (Betroffenenrechte, Art. 12–22) as its own block — at minimum the request channel and, for this site without user accounts, a short 'nicht einschlägig' for deletion/export — rather than skipping it

evals.name: static-site-runtime-scan
evals.prompt: Hier ist eine fertige statische Kundenseite (reines HTML) im Ordner tests/fixtures/site-accept-order — serve sie lokal (z. B. python3 -m http.server) und prüf sie auf Datenschutz, inklusive Laufzeitverhalten des Cookie-Banners. Kurzbericht reicht.
evals.expected_output: The executor serves the folder, runs scripts/scan-origins.mjs against it, and reports from the scan: nothing third-party before consent, the reject button works, Hotjar loads only after 'Alle akzeptieren' (so it is a consent-gated service that the DSE must list), the first layer offers a reject option. The report says which page was scanned and that one scan is one page.
expectations: The runtime scanner scripts/scan-origins.mjs is executed against a locally served URL (visible in the transcript), not replaced by reading the HTML only
The report states that no third-party origin is contacted before consent (🟢 for that item), based on the scan's pre-consent phase

Hotjar (static.hotjar.com) is identified as loading only after 'Alle akzeptieren' and is listed as a consent-required service (§ 25 TDDDG, Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. a) that belongs in the Datenschutzerklärung — with the session-recording risk note
The report confirms that the first layer has a reject option ('Nur notwendige akzeptieren') and that no new third-party requests fire after it
The report notes that the accept phase clicked 'Alle akzeptieren' (not the 'Nur notwendige' button) — i.e. the service inventory is complete
The report says which page and which states were scanned (vor Einwilligung, nach Ablehnen, nach Akzeptieren) and that subpages need their own scan

The report names the state after withdrawal of consent (nach Widerruf) as not scanned — whether withdrawing removes the Hotjar cookie and stops the script is open; a recommendation to 'also test withdrawal' without saying it was not covered fails
The missing /impressum and /datenschutz pages (404 in the scan) are flagged as 🔴 — links exist but the targets do not
The output ends with the RDG disclaimer and does not call the site 'abmahnsicher'

Evidence levels match the scan: only what the scan JSON shows (requests, origins, clicked button, HTTP status) is beobachtet; consequences not visible in the scan — Hotjar session recording actually running, persistence across reloads, what Hotjar collects — are marked abgeleitet

evals.name: praxis-art9-intake
evals.prompt: Ein Kunde (Praxis für ästhetische Chirurgie) hat mir nur diese eine Seite geschickt: evals/files/praxis-booking/termin.html. Er fragt, ob das so okay ist und ob ich die Datenschutzerklärung dafür schreiben kann.
evals.expected_output: The executor recognises Art. 9 health data from the form fields (Behandlung select, Beschwerden/Vorerkrankungen/Medikamente textarea, photo upload), classifies Formspree and Calendly as US services in the health-data path (🔴 under the conservative rule, marked as rule, with the lawyer-exception note), cites § 203 StGB, Art. 9(2)(a)/(h) + § 22 BDSG, DSFA and DSB questions — and does NOT write a Datenschutzerklärung yet: it asks the intake questions (Phase 2) first, because Verantwortlicher, Kammer, hosting, processors are unknown.
expectations: The response identifies the form as collecting Art. 9 data (health), naming at least the 'Beschwerden / Vorerkrankungen / Medikamente' field, the treatment select and the photo upload as the reasons

Formspree as the form target is 🔴 for Art. 9 content and explicitly marked as a conservative rule (R / 'konservative Regel'), with the note that a lawyer can sign off an exception (DPF + AVV + TIA + § 203-Absicherung)
Calendly is treated the same way: 🔴 for a Heilberuf under the rule, Art. 9 in the booking subject, with an EU/self-hosted alternative named (e.g. Cal.com self-hosted or an EU booking tool)
§ 203 StGB (Berufsgeheimnis) and Art. 9 Abs. 2 lit. a / lit. h DSGVO i. V. m. § 22 BDSG are cited as the legal frame
DSFA (Art. 35) and DSB (Art. 37 Abs. 1 lit. c / § 38 BDSG) are raised as questions or findings, not silently skipped
The Calendly widget.js loaded on page load (script tag at the end of termin.html, before any user action) is flagged as a third-party load before any consent (🔴)
No Datenschutzerklärung is generated in this turn; instead the Phase-2 intake questions are asked in one batch (Verantwortlicher, Kammer/Berufsbezeichnung, hosting, processors/AVVs, DSB, retention)
The response does not invent a Kammer, register number, or hosting provider for the practice

The response distinguishes 'rechtswidrig' from 'konservative Regel' in its wording, and the final chat answer (not only a report file) contains the RDG disclaimer or an explicit 'keine Rechtsberatung (RDG)' line

Every concrete vendor fact — whether from web research or from memory (e.g. Formspree storage location or retention, Calendly DPA availability, DPF status) — carries a source with a date or is explicitly marked as to be verified; a vendor fact stated as plain fact without either fails

The § 203 StGB point covers every service provider that can see the content — hoster, form backend or booking tool, mailbox provider and the agency with admin access — with the confidentiality obligation of § 203 Abs. 4 StGB, not only the US services

The DSFA/DSB assessment is proportionate and cites ErwG 91 for both: a single physician's practice is usually not 'umfangreich', so the response asks for a documented threshold analysis (Schwellwertanalyse) and the facts that would change it (Anzahl Personen, § 38 BDSG 20-Personen-Schwelle) — an open DSFA/DSB question rated 🟠 or 🔴, or 'DSFA durchführen' / 'im Zweifel DSB bestellen' as the recommendation, fails

The response notices that the form in termin.html has no enctype="multipart/form-data", so as written the browser sends only the file name, not the photo — and states that the photo would reach Formspree (Art. 9 image data) once the form is fixed; a response that states as fact that the photo currently reaches Formspree fails

evals.name: astro-minimal-dse-generation
evals.prompt: Schreib die Datenschutzerklärung und das Impressum für diese Astro-Seite einer Tischlerei. Code: evals/files/astro-minimal. Die Intake-Antworten des Kunden stehen in evals/files/astro-minimal/INTAKE.md.
evals.expected_output: Two German files: a Datenschutzerklärung containing only the modules the evidence supports (Verantwortlicher, Allgemeines, Hosting Hetzner + Server-Logs 7 Tage, Cookies/Endgerät with 'keine einwilligungsbedürftigen', Kontaktformular with the exact fields and the mailbox as recipient, Plausible on Art. 6(1)(f) with the EU note, Rechte incl. highlighted Art. 21, Beschwerderecht naming LDI NRW, Datensicherheit, Pflicht zur Bereitstellung, keine automatisierte Entscheidung, Stand), and an Impressum with the intake data. No [PLATZHALTER] left in either file; anything genuinely unknown is listed in the chat message instead.
expectations: A Datenschutzerklärung file and an Impressum file are written (German)
Neither delivered file contains the string '[PLATZHALTER]' or any unfilled [BRACKET] placeholder from the templates; unknown items, if any, are listed in the chat message

The Datenschutzerklärung contains NO module for Google Fonts, Google Analytics, YouTube, Maps, Newsletter, Bewerbungen, Nutzerkonto, Zahlungen or KI — none of these exist in the code (fonts are @fontsource, i.e. self-hosted)
Plausible is described on Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. f DSGVO as cookieless with the berechtigtes Interesse named, EU hosting and the DPA mentioned — not on consent, and not omitted
Hosting names Hetzner Online GmbH with the AVV, server-log fields, and the 7-day retention from INTAKE.md

The Kontaktformular module lists the fields in kontakt.astro (Name, E-Mail, Nachricht) and no other form field — derived metadata such as the time of sending is fine, the honeypot must not be listed as a data field — names the mailbox/SMTP as the recipient, Art. 6 Abs. 1 lit. b/f, and the 6-month retention from INTAKE.md
The cookies section states that no consent-requiring cookies or storage are used (no CMP needed) — consistent with the code
The Art. 21 Widerspruchsrecht is visually highlighted (blockquote/bold) and the Beschwerderecht names the LDI NRW as the supervisory authority for a Solingen company

The Impressum contains the HRB number, Amtsgericht Wuppertal, USt-IdNr., Vertretungsberechtigter and no OS-Plattform link; the § 36 VSBG sentence is present or its omission is justified by ≤ 10 employees
The Datenschutzerklärung contains the 'Pflicht zur Bereitstellung' statement (Art. 13(2)(e): which fields are required for the contact form and what happens without them)
Both files carry a Stand date; the RDG note is delivered either in the chat answer or in a block inside the file that is clearly marked as internal / not for publication

No client fact is filled in that neither INTAKE.md nor the code states: no Handwerkskammer, Berufsbezeichnung, Aufsichtsbehörde for the trade or VSBG willingness ('bereit' / 'nicht bereit') inferred from location or trade — missing mandatory items are asked for instead

Technical claims in the Datenschutzerklärung that the code and INTAKE.md do not prove (e.g. 'Die Website wird über HTTPS/TLS ausgeliefert' — the code only proves TLS for SMTP) are either left out or listed in the chat answer as 'vor Veröffentlichung prüfen'; per SKILL.md Phase 5 a claim that is listed there passes, an unlisted one fails

evals.name: ai-chatbot-processor
evals.prompt: Wir haben auf der Website einer Steuerberatung einen Chat-Assistenten mit OpenAI eingebaut (Code in evals/files/nextjs-ai-chat). Ist das datenschutzrechtlich okay so? Was müssen wir ändern?
evals.expected_output: The executor treats the OpenAI API as an Auftragsverarbeiter (DPA/API terms, no training, retention, region/DPF check to be verified via WebSearch), flags the missing Art. 50 KI-VO labelling (the UI says 'Unser Team antwortet sofort' — misleading; in force since 02.08.2026), flags the triage ('einfach/komplex/abgelehnt') as a potential Art. 22 decision needing human review, the unlimited chat_logs retention in Supabase with the service-role key, the localStorage session id (§ 25 TDDDG technically necessary or not — justify), the risk of Art. 9-adjacent inputs (tax situation can reveal health, religion, union — Kirchensteuer!), and asks for a KI module in the DSE.
expectations: OpenAI is classified as an Auftragsverarbeiter (Art. 28) with the four checks named: DPA/API terms, no training on inputs, retention (zero-data-retention or a stated period), region/transfer mechanism (DPF status of the entity to be verified, not assumed)

The response raises the Berufsgeheimnis of a Steuerberatung — § 203 Abs. 1 Nr. 3 StGB and § 62a StBerG (written confidentiality obligation of the service provider, beyond the AVV) — as a reason why OpenAI and Supabase need more than a DPA

The UI text 'Unser Team antwortet sofort' is flagged: the chatbot is not labelled as AI — Art. 50 KI-VO (in force since 02.08.2026) requires that users are told they are interacting with an AI system, and the response proposes concrete label text
The triage into 'einfach / komplex / abgelehnt' is identified as a potential Art. 22 DSGVO automated decision (esp. 'abgelehnt') and human review / DSE disclosure is required
The unlimited storage of full transcripts in Supabase chat_logs is flagged (no retention/deletion, Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. e), with a concrete retention proposal

The response notes that tax-related chat input can carry special-category data (e.g. Kirchensteuer → religion; Behinderten-Pauschbetrag → health) and applies the conservative rule for Art. 9 input to a US LLM, marked as a rule

The KI-Funktion is covered in the Datenschutzerklärung either by a delivered draft module or by an explicit list naming all six items: provider, purpose, data categories, retention, third-country transfer, and the Art. 22 statement on the triage
The localStorage 'chat-session' key is assessed under § 25 TDDDG with a justification either way (technically necessary for the chosen function vs. not)

Every concrete OpenAI retention or residency fact (e.g. 30-day abuse-monitoring logs, eu.api.openai.com / EU data residency, zero-data-retention prerequisites) carries either a fetched vendor source with a retrieval date or an explicit 'verify' mark on that fact — a generic 'beim Anbieter prüfen' footnote while the table states the fact plainly fails
The final chat answer contains the RDG disclaimer (not only the report's section 8) and does not call the setup 'konform' without conditions

Any statement about the DPF status of OpenAI or Supabase is either absent (replaced by 'verify on dataprivacyframework.gov/list for the specific entity') or taken from that official list with a date — no DPF verdict built on a secondary website

evals.name: member-portal-rights
evals.prompt: Unser Kunde, ein Yogastudio, bekommt einen Mitgliederbereich mit Konto, Kursbuchung, Zahlungen über Stripe und Newsletter (Next.js + Supabase). Der Code liegt in evals/files/nextjs-member-portal. Bitte vor dem Launch auf Datenschutz prüfen und den Audit-Bericht schreiben.
evals.expected_output: A German audit report in the Phase-4 structure that traces the account lifecycle, not only the forms: the 'Konto löschen' route deletes only the profiles row (auth user, avatars and invoice PDFs in Storage, Brevo contact, Stripe customer and Sentry user context remain) while the cascade hard-deletes invoices that must be kept (§ 147 AO / § 257 HGB → Sperrung, Art. 17 Abs. 3 lit. b / Art. 18). The DSE promise of complete deletion contradicts the code. The health-notes field is Art. 9. Newsletter mails have no unsubscribe link or List-Unsubscribe header, there is no persistent Cookie-Einstellungen link, no data export, and rights requests go only to a contact form. Correctly gated Meta Pixel is not reported as a pre-consent load. Evidence level: code only.
expectations: A report file matching datenschutz-audit-*.md is written with the eight Phase-4 sections in order, and its Prüftabelle has a Betroffenenrechte block (Art. 12–22) that assesses deletion, access/export, rectification, objection/withdrawal and the request channel individually

The delete flow in app/api/account/delete/route.ts is flagged (🔴 or 🟠, Art. 17) because it deletes only the profiles row: the Supabase auth user in auth.users remains (the FK cascades from auth.users to profiles, not the other way), so e-mail and login survive — with the file reference
The report states that Storage objects are not deleted: the avatar (avatar_path, bucket 'avatars') and the invoice PDFs (pdf_path, bucket 'invoices') remain after 'Konto löschen'
The report states that deletion does not reach the recipients (Art. 17 Abs. 2 / Art. 19): at least the Brevo contact and the Stripe customer are named, and preferably the Sentry user context

The report identifies the opposite problem in the same flow: ON DELETE CASCADE hard-deletes invoices that are subject to retention duties (§ 147 AO and/or § 257 HGB), and recommends restriction/blocking (Art. 18 or Art. 17 Abs. 3 lit. b) with a Löschkonzept instead of immediate deletion

The sentence in app/datenschutz/page.tsx that all data is 'vollständig und unwiderruflich entfernt' is flagged as contradicting the code (inaccurate information, Art. 12/13), and a corrected statement is proposed or required

The 'gesundheitshinweise' field (Verletzungen, Schwangerschaft) is recognised as Art. 9 health data needing explicit consent (Art. 9 Abs. 2 lit. a) or an equivalent basis, voluntary (optional field or opt-in), with access limited to the teachers — and the report notes where it can survive account deletion or needs its own retention (Sentry events with sendDefaultPii, backups, no deletion period while the account exists)

The missing self-service export or documented access procedure (Art. 15, Art. 20) is flagged or asked as an open question, and rectification (Art. 16) via the profile form in app/konto/page.tsx is noted as present

Newsletter: sendMonthly in lib/newsletter.ts sends without an unsubscribe link and without a List-Unsubscribe header — flagged with Art. 21 Abs. 2/3 DSGVO and/or Art. 7 Abs. 3 and § 7 UWG; the missing double opt-in in subscribe() is flagged as well

Consent withdrawal (Art. 7 Abs. 3) is flagged: the footer has no persistent 'Cookie-Einstellungen' link and the banner cannot be reopened once a choice is stored — while the Meta Pixel itself is correctly reported as loading only after 'Alle akzeptieren', not as a pre-consent load
The request channel is flagged: the DSE sends rights requests only to a contact form with no e-mail address or other channel named (Art. 12 Abs. 1–3)

Row Level Security is flagged: 001_init.sql enables RLS only on profiles, so bookings and invoices (with the service-role and anon clients) are readable across members unless policies exist — Art. 32 / Art. 5 Abs. 1 lit. f, with the file reference
Sentry with sendDefaultPii: true and Sentry.setUser({ email }) in app/layout.tsx is flagged as personal data in error tracking, with Sentry as a processor whose AVV status is open

The Management Summary states the evidence level as code only (no runtime scan, no live URL), every 🔴/🟠 finding has an E-xx evidence line with a level, and the report ends with the RDG disclaimer without calling the portal 'konform' or 'abmahnsicher'
